title: Q-CTRL Demonstrates Push-Button Cold-Start Calibration on QuantWare Superconducting QPUs - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Q-CTRL's Boulder Opal autonomously brought up a 21-qubit QuantWare Contralto-D21 from cold start, reaching 99.95% median single-qubit and 96% median (>98% peak) two-qubit CZ fidelity in under three hours per five-qubit feedline, replacing multi-day manual tuning.

themes.theme: Autonomous bring-up benchmarks on QuantWare D-Line

insights.claim: Q-CTRL's Boulder Opal autonomously tuned five-qubit feedline blocks of a 21-qubit QuantWare Contralto-D21 superconducting processor from an uncalibrated state to operational gate fidelities in under three hours without manual specialist intervention.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Calibration time collapsing from days to hours lowers operating cost and raises uptime for superconducting QPU vendors.
insights.quote: tuned five-qubit feedline blocks from an uncalibrated state to operational gate fidelities in under three hours without manual specialist intervention
insights.locator: Quantum infrastructure software provider Q-CTRL has

insights.claim: Autonomous calibration by Q-CTRL Boulder Opal on a QuantWare Contralto-D21 achieved a 99.95% median single-qubit (SX) gate fidelity.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Automated tuning matching expert-level single-qubit fidelity removes a key argument for in-house physicist teams.

insights.claim: Two-qubit CZ gate fidelity after Boulder Opal's autonomous calibration of the QuantWare Contralto-D21 reached >98% at peak but only 96% as a device median.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The 96% median two-qubit fidelity shows automation solves bring-up labor but not the underlying hardware quality gap to error-correction thresholds.

insights.claim: Q-CTRL positions its <3-hour cold-start bring-up per 5-qubit feedline as replacing multi-day manual tuning cycles across resonator mapping and qubit discovery.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Order-of-magnitude reduction in bring-up time is a scaling enabler for OEM chip suppliers like QuantWare selling to third-party integrators.
insights.quote: Replaces multi-day manual tuning cycles across resonator mapping and qubit discovery

themes.theme: Calibration as the superconducting scaling bottleneck

insights.claim: Scaling superconducting quantum computers is bottlenecked operationally because dozens of interdependent control parameters, from TWPA biases to qubit drive frequencies and flux pulses, must be iteratively tuned and stabilized against environmental drift.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Control/calibration software is a structural chokepoint as qubit counts grow, creating a durable software layer opportunity.
insights.quote: Scaling superconducting quantum computers presents a severe operational bottleneck

insights.claim: Conventional scripted calibration routines frequently fail when superconducting hardware frequencies drift outside narrow scan windows, forcing experimental physicists to intervene manually.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Failure modes of scripted calibration explain why AI/state-machine approaches can command a premium.
insights.quote: Conventional scripted calibration routines frequently fail when hardware frequencies drift outside narrow scan windows

insights.claim: Boulder Opal encodes architecture-specific calibration routines into an automated physics-informed AI state machine that detects out-of-range anomalies, filters false-positive resonances and autonomously recovers underperforming qubits, logging parameter histories and waveforms to a web dashboard.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Architecture-specific encoding implies per-vendor integration work, which builds switching costs for Q-CTRL across hardware partners.

insights.claim: Q-CTRL plans to extend Boulder Opal autonomous calibration to the QuantWare A-Line with tunable-coupler support, task parallelization and continuous runtime drift tracking in late 2026.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Continuous drift tracking would turn calibration from a one-off bring-up tool into recurring runtime software revenue.
insights.quote: Adds tunable-coupler support, task parallelization, and continuous drift tracking in late 2026

insights.claim: Q-CTRL is pursuing autonomous calibration integrations with multiple superconducting hardware makers, including QuantWare and Anyon Technologies for enterprise data centers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A hardware-agnostic calibration layer across vendors positions Q-CTRL as an infrastructure 'picks and shovels' play.
